summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of spinal gunshot wound, neurogenic bladder, and homelessness was admitted for right flank pain. She expressed regret for leaving a prior admission early and wished to stay for full evaluation. Workup showed no evidence of nephrolithiasis or pyelonephritis on renal ultrasound, and labs did not support active infection despite a positive urine culture likely reflecting colonization. Blood cultures did not show recurrent Corynebacterium bacteremia. Flank pain improved with NSAIDs and acetaminophen with codeine. She was treated with a single dose of fluconazole for vaginal candidiasis and continued home medications for frostbite. Social work secured shelter placement. She was discharged home with naproxen for pain and instructions to return if symptoms worsened.
problems: Late effect of spinal cord injury
Late effects of injury purposely inflicted by other person
